# FRAMEWORK-IMPROVEMENTS — suggestions for cap-evolve itself (cross-run)

NOT about this capability or this run's result — about what cap-evolve the FRAMEWORK should change so FUTURE runs (any capability, any project) go better: a confusing prompt section, a missing tool, a file you wished existed, a gate that felt wrong. Optional most iterations; add an entry whenever something about the framework itself (not the task) got in your way or surprised you.

## From run_20260909_092628 iteration 1
- **Surface sibling runs in RUNMAP.** LEDGER/RUNMAP/`rejected.jsonl` were all empty at iteration 1, yet `.capevolve/run_20260909_005053/` had already refuted the most obvious version of my main hypothesis (val 0.850, Δ −0.040). I found it only by grepping the wider repo. Prior runs against the SAME capability should be listed in RUNMAP as read-only prior art, or at least pointed at.
- **The two prior-run journal entries were framework-synthesized stubs** ("⚠ EMPTY HANDOVER — the optimizer wrote no entry of its own"), so the only recoverable signal was the gate's one-line reason plus the candidate diffs. Worth failing an iteration louder when JOURNAL.md is left unwritten, since that entry is the whole cross-iteration memory.
- **Give the optimizer the reward decomposition.** Fitting weights from `trajectories/*.json` was the single highest-value step (it showed `rfe_quality` holds 56% of headroom and that 1 boolean = 2 `rfe_quality` points), but it is guesswork that every iteration must redo. Publishing per-judge weights + current means in INSTRUCTIONS.md would make every iteration better targeted.
- **`validate()` is not runnable locally.** INSTRUCTIONS.md says "Check `rfe-skill-pipeline`'s `validate()` output before finalizing", but `skillsaw` is not installed and no entrypoint exists in the repo, so I could only re-implement the byte-budget check by hand. Either ship a runnable `validate` command or state that byte counts are the checkable part.
- **Flag environment-vs-capability defects.** The largest structural failure was that `subagent_type: rfe-scorer` does not exist in the eval environment. The capability can only work around it. Telling the optimizer which referenced resources are actually absent at runtime would prevent wasted iterations trying to make the intended path work.
